doc.title: Joe Muranyi interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2007

title: Traveling with an integrated band and a visit from Vince Giordano
summary: Asked about integrated travel with Armstrong, he says it was never an issue, after a brief interruption by a visitor.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Yeah. Did you ever have any issues with traveling in an integrated group when you were with Louis?
No.
We’ll take a short pause here. I think this is a fellow you might know actually.
Who’s that.
Hi come on in.
Oh Joe Muranyi, don’t believe anything he says.
I’m trying not to.
Hey did you get my email?
Is this on the film?
This is on the film now.
Oh Jesus I’m sorry.
That’s all right. We’re just wrapping up. You guys can just — we’re a little cramped here. TH: We were supposed to have a suite and this is what we have.
Great to see you, Vinnie, I think you deserve to be interviewed man. © Fillius Jazz Archive -24-
Well I don’t know about that.
Yeah, go on.
I’m trying to remember what we were talking about.
About jazz, about liking jazz or not liking jazz. Well there was some factor you were going to.
The jazz education we were talking about — oh I know, I was just wondering about when you traveled with Louis, that the group was integrated, if it ever became an issue traveling anywhere.
You mean the fact that he was black or that it was a mixed band?
Yes, it was a mixed band.

No. By the time I was there, I heard him refer, he’d meet some of his old buddies would come up and there was one he was talking about, I had $2,000 in my pocket, he said, and I had no place to sleep or eat or anything. So that came up, but art, you know, art actually.
